chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Khalid al-Maraghi reported to me, he said: Thawabah ibn Yazid narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Ali ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Shababah ibn Sawwar, he said: al-Mubarak ibn Saeed narrated to me, from Khalil al-Farra, from Abu al-Mujabbar, who said:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, said: "Four things corrupt the hearts: seclusion with women, listening to them, adopting their opinions, and keeping company with the dead."
So it was said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, what is keeping company with the dead?" He said: "Keeping company with anyone who has strayed from the faith and is unjust in judgments."

key_terms.الخلوة: Seclusion, being alone in private -- an Islamic legal and ethical concept
key_terms.جائر في الأحكام: Unjust in judgments -- one who rules unfairly
key_terms.ضال عن الإيمان: One who has strayed from faith
key_terms.مجالسة الموتى: Keeping company with the dead -- a metaphor for associating with spiritually corrupt individuals
key_terms.مفسدة: Corrupting, causing ruin -- describes things that deteriorate the spiritual state of the heart

ai.seo_question: What are the four things that corrupt the heart according to Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: The Prophet (SAWW), as transmitted through a chain of narrators in the Amali of al-Mufid, enumerated four things that corrupt the hearts. Three relate to uncritical private interactions with women -- seclusion, listening to their counsel, and adopting their opinions -- reflecting concerns about improper influence in the social norms of 7th-century Arabia. The fourth, "company of the dead," is a striking metaphor: the Prophet clarified it means associating with those who have deviated from faith or act unjustly in their rulings, as such people are spiritually dead despite being physically alive.
